initial: Create a polished, publication-quality scientific architecture figure for the paper DEBR (Dual-Experience Behavioral Retention), lifelong robot imitation learning. Wide landscape aspect ratio, white background, restrained blue/teal/orange palette, thin clean arrows, generous whitespace, crisp Times New Roman serif English lettering, no gradients, no decorative title banner, no watermark, no invented experimental results. This is a precise conceptual diagram, not a chart. Make text legible and concise. Scientific invariants: CADL = Coverage-Aware Demonstration Learning, combines RA-Coreset and Execution Supervision. SHBR = Successful Historical Behavior Retention. Current task demonstrations plus stored old expert demonstrations supply base learning loss L_C. After learning a task, fixed-budget autonomous collection retains SUCCESSFUL trajectories only, recording latent histories H and fixed Gaussian behavior references (mu_T, sigma_T); no old teacher network is retained. Each task's support q_j is number of independent contributing successful trajectories divided by fixed collection count N_roll. SHBR uses task-balanced slots and fixed denominator to form L_SHBR. Retention candidate objective L_Q = L_C + lambda_R L_SHBR. Later-task gate compares TWO candidates generated from THE SAME full starting state (model, optimizer, scheduler, RNG) and SAME main-batch sequence, each B=10 updates; they are alternative branches, not sequential updates. On fixed TRAINING probes accept retention candidate Q ONLY if all three hold: BC_Q <= BC_C; Exec_Q <= Exec_C; Ret_Q < Ret_C. Otherwise select base C. Commit the selected COMPLETE state. First incremental task uses base update only. Stage-end demonstration memory and successful-history memory feed the NEXT task, never suggest collection happens inside every optimization block. All added memories and gate are training-only; deployment retains original policy inference. Use mathematical subscripts where possible. Avoid claiming global optimality or guarantees of closed-loop success. VERSION A: dual-experience parallel lanes. A visually balanced horizontal left-to-right architecture. Top lane blue labeled "CADL | Expert demonstrations" with compact steps "Current demonstrations + Replay", "RA-Coreset" (small illustrative protected random anchors plus coverage exchange), "Execution supervision", output "Base objective L_C". Bottom lane teal labeled "SHBR | Successful experience" with small memory stack labeled "Latent histories + Fixed Gaussian references", "Task support q_j", "Support-weighted retention", output "L_SHBR". At right a shared orange framed panel labeled "Candidate-update gate": clearly depict same state Omega splitting to Base C and Retention Q, training probes, three inequalities stacked, chosen state. Thin dashed return arrows at bottom labeled "At task end: update memories for the next task" originate from learned stage policy, with distinct paths to demonstration memory and successful collection. A small deployment box separate at far right: "Original policy inference". Overall figure should be concise enough for a two-column journal width. Do not overfill. Bottom centered caption "(A) Dual-experience architecture".

Replace task support formula by plain two-line text "q_j = n_j^+ / N_roll" and "Independent successful trajectories contributing to cache". Replace the incorrect 1/J sum in support-weighted retention box by EXACT formula "L_SHBR = (1/B_R) Σ_(i=1)^(B_R) q_(j_i) l_ret(ξ_i)" in properly typeset form with descriptive line "Fixed slot denominator B_R; empty slots contribute zero". At bottom memory feedback explicitly show learned stage policy -> "At task end: fixed-budget rollouts; retain successes only" -> successful-history memory -> SHBR for next task. Make both Select Q and Select C flow into a single "Commit selected full state" before learned policy. Include small text "First task: base updates only". Keep three correct gate inequalities. Remove any scene art that impairs clarity. Avoid adding new mechanisms.
